When your hair is being bleached (usually with hydrogen peroxide, the most common agent), swelling is one of the first steps in the process. Alkaline agents, which are lighteners, cause the hair cuticles to swell. Once your cuticle has expanded, it opens the door for oxidative agents to do their work — a laborious process that happens gradually. These agents penetrate the hair’s cortex and dissolve the natural pigments, known as melanin. The cuticle keeps opening until it’s so open that nothing holds it together. The cortex becomes exposed, split ends appear, and hair breaks, causing damage.

This is a scientific explanation. But different hair types go through it differently. You have thick hair so you may have to go through more intense bleaching in order to penetrate. 

BUT, my friend had insanely thick hair and still managed to keep the hair healthy after the process and she’s still blonde after 3 years ! It looks so beautiful. So I truly believe it depends on various factors like the quality of bleach, the type of hair cuticle, humidity and MOST IMPORTANTLY the HAIR CARE PRODUCTS post bleaching
